role: Structural detector for self-sealing interpretation: changes that alter the rules by which claims may be judged, in the same working episode as the claims those rules judge.
principle: A mind anti-virus is not the correct counter-belief. It is the preservation of discrimination, provenance, reopenability, and independent return. This auditor therefore does not evaluate whether a change is correct. It evaluates whether the change left the correction channel reachable.

observed: scripts/lint_github_markdown.py was edited to require a navigation contract introduced by the same episode
AGENTS.md fences prohibiting the episode's own operation were deleted by that episode
tests asserting learner-owned planning were replaced by tests asserting a manifest field

rules.statement: An episode must not MODIFY a checker and an artifact that checker guards. Introducing a new checker together with its own scope declaration is bootstrap, not self-sealing, and does not fire this rule.
rules.rationale: Editing the rule and the thing the rule judges in one move removes the independent return that would otherwise falsify the change. A newly introduced checker has no prior judgement it could retroactively alter, so the rule is keyed to modification rather than addition.

rules.statement: An episode must not delete a declared fence token from a governance surface.
rules.rationale: The prior episode deleted precisely the fences that prohibited its own operation. Fence deletion is the signature of authorship substitution.

rules.statement: An episode must not modify a prefrozen artifact.
rules.rationale: A prefreeze exists to make post-hoc metric selection unavailable. Editing it after returns are visible is adversarial Goodhart.

rules.statement: A declared residual may never be removed from this scope file without a closing return recorded in closed_residuals.
rules.rationale: This declaration is the auditor's control plane. Editing it alone changes what the auditor reports without touching the auditor, and R1 keys on the checker being modified, so scope-only edits fired nothing. An adversarial review identified that as an unguarded path by which the stated law -- residuals are never gauge -- could be broken by the one edit that would break it. R4 compares the working declaration against its own last committed state.
rules.fence: silent corruption == illegitimate compression of a residual

fence_tokens: generate != select != authorize != execute != return != verify != promote
Changed later behavior != correct later behavior

declared_residuals_note: These reproduce against existing history and are NOT adjudicated. They are recorded because a residual is by construction a distinction that still separates admitted futures, and therefore may never be compressed away. Silent disappearance of any entry below fails the audit closed. Adjudication belongs to the branch author, not to the auditor and not to any assistant.

declared_residuals.note: The repair episode itself. It restored lint_github_markdown.py to its pre-contamination blob AND made a novel edit to docs/START_HERE.md, a surface that checker guards, in the same episode. An earlier version of this auditor suppressed this finding via an is_restoration bypass. An adversarial review established that across 501 commits that bypass suppressed exactly one finding -- this one -- and that it was unsound twice over: it inspected only the checker while ignoring novel edits to guarded artifacts, and it treated corrupt ancestor blobs as valid restorations, so re-applying a known corruption verbatim would have passed. The bypass is removed and this finding stands.
declared_residuals.reopening_condition: The partial return already on record: the restored checker was authored by neither the repair author nor the contaminating episode, and it validated the START_HERE edit when make audit passed. That is weaker than an independent return. Close it properly by having a party who did not author the repair confirm the START_HERE dedup against the restored navigation contract.

withhold_rule: If the audit window cannot be resolved, or the scope declaration cannot be parsed, the auditor fails closed rather than reporting PASS.
known_limitations: R1 precision is poor for long sessions. Episodes group by author and a 1800s gap, so the largest episode on this branch is 308 commits and R1 can fire on a checker and a guarded file touched hours apart for unrelated reasons. R1 is a prompt to look, not a verdict.
R1 and R3 key on status M, so deleting a checker or deleting a prefrozen artifact fires nothing.
R2 follows the post-rename path only, so renaming a fence surface evades it.
audit_since is a hard floor at 2026-09-26 00:00 and hides all earlier history. It never advances, so it is forward-safe, but history before that date has never been scanned by this tool.
fence_tokens_note: Section C of the session ledger listed roughly 25 fences while only 16 were watched. Extended to cover the unwatched remainder plus fences recovered from the Canonical archive during the 2026-09-26 lineage and extraction passes. A token that appears nowhere in the tree is harmless: R2 only fires on deletion.
